title: Grateful Dead Live at The Spectrum on 1973-09-21
lineage: SBD -> Rm -> Reel -> PCM -> DatTransfer Info: Dat (Sony R500) -> Samplitude v6.0 -> Cool Edit Pro v1.2 -> CD -> EAC -> SHN

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard capture of a high‑energy 9/21/73 show with smoking Let It Grow, horns‑rich He's Gone > Truckin' > The Other One sequence and standouts like Big Railroad Blues, Wharf Rat and Row Jimmy.
ai_review.review: The recording is a generally clear soundboard source that delivers the band’s 1973 fire with only occasional hiss and brief cuts.  Fans rave about the horn‑filled second half – especially Let It Grow, the seamless He's Gone → Truckin' → The Other One medley, and powerhouse moments on Big Railroad Blues, Wharf Rat and Row Jimmy.  Overall the performance is tight, lively and showcases Jerry’s soaring soloing while Bill Kreutzmann drives a solid rhythmic foundation.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews rate the show 4‑5 stars, praising both musical performance and recording clarity; only minor criticisms (hiss, occasional cuts) keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp and clear overall with a slight hiss compared to other '73 boards; a few painful cuts at the end of Playin' but no major drop‑outs. Bass and piano sit low in the mix for some listeners.

standout_songs: He's Gone > Truckin' > The Other One > Wharf Rat > Row Jimmy
poor_songs: "Let Me Sing Your Blues Away" (noted as a weaker bar tune)
Vocals off in spots on some numbers
show_quality.setlist_flow: A tight, typical early‑'73 first set followed by a horn‑enhanced second half; the horns join after the opening of Set 2, adding extra sparkle to Let It Grow and the jammed medley.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for beautiful tone, feeling no pain, and a superb solo on Row Jimmy; described as 'as always' and 'beautiful'.
band_member_comments.Keys: Horn section highlighted – Joe Ellis (trumpet) and Martin Fierro (sax) are noted as adding great texture; Keith (Ellis) is mentioned as being very ‘up’ for the show.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann singled out as awesome, clean in the mix with excellent snare/kick interaction; Mickey’s presence is minimal in this recording.
